text:
maria: heads-up — HF->Redwood convert for community/model-x failed on our pipeline during onboarding. convertbot shows a safetensors shard/index mismatch and the chat template's <|sys|> token is missing after convert.

convertbot: conversion error for community/model-x@main: safetensors shard index mismatch (index.json lists 3 shards, found 2). fallback attempted, but tokenizer special tokens dropped. stack: KeyError("weight_name_map['lm_head']")
```
ERROR: safetensors.index: expected 3 shards, found 2
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/convert/runner.py", line 214, in run
    load_shards(index)
  File "/app/convert/safetensors.py", line 98, in load_shards
    raise IndexMismatchError(msg)
safetensors.index.IndexMismatchError: index.json lists 3 shards but 2 files found
```

devin: did we pin the hub revision when the model was uploaded? this sounds like a hub snapshot race where index.json was updated but shards weren't replicated yet.

maria: we passed revision pin `main@2025-03-02-13:10` to the converter. pipeline logs show a 200 from hub but the returned index had `metadata.num_shards: 3` while only two shards downloaded. snippet: `GET /models/community/model-x/main@2025-03-02-13:10/index.json -> 200` then later `GET .../shard-2.safetensors -> 404`.

luis: two issues here that interact: 1) converter currently silently strips special tokens referenced only in `model_card.config.chat_templates` if they aren't present in tokenizer files; we then end up with chatfmt mismatches. 2) safetensors index mismatch should fail hard and not attempt a partial merge — partial merge is what triggered a weight-key remapping pass that renamed `transformer.wte` -> `tok_embeddings` and that rename wasn't compatible with our kv-cache name expectations.

rachael: we also saw weight key renames in a previous import where HF `lm_head` was saved as `lm_head.weight` in a shard and convertbot's autoremapping dropped the suffix. that broke our quantization pipeline because the quant tool expects exact key names for per-layer config.

patrick: agreed on fixes. short list: (a) treat shard count mismatch as fatal; (b) add `--preserve-special-tokens` to converter which injects missing special tokens into tokenizer vocab with synthetic ids (and emits a warning) instead of dropping them; (c) add an explicit weight-key-remap manifest opt-in rather than auto-rename; (d) fail fast on hub auth 401/403 and retry logic with exponential backoff + revision verification. i'll open a PR.

maria: repro steps for the team:
1) checkout `infra/convert` @ `3f2c9d6`
2) run `./convert --model community/model-x --revision main@2025-03-02-13:10 --out redwood/model-x`
3) observe index download then `safetensors.index.IndexMismatchError` and tokenizer missing `<|sys|>` from `config.json` chat_templates

devin: quick workaround for onboarding now?

luis: you can re-run convert with `--revision main@<commit_sha>` where commit_sha is the exact commit the uploader used (not just a branch pin). if hub auth was flaky, regenerate temp creds; also we have a small script `tools/ensure_shards.py` that validates index vs actual shard files before convert. use that until the fix lands.

patrick: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convert/pull/3421 — changes: fail on index mismatch, --preserve-special-tokens flag, weight-remap manifest opt-in, clearer log for hub revision verification. tests added for safetensors index and tokenizer-preserve behavior.

convertbot: deploy triggered: convert-service/staging -> started by patrick (ci/convert-build#578).

maria: re-ran with exact commit pin and regenerated creds; shards all present and convert completed, but our eval suite shows a small quality regression (assistant turns have +0.6 perplexity) — likely caused by the autoremapped weight keys + baseline quant profile mismatch. planning an A/B with quant-profile `gptq-8g-128` vs `gptq-8g-64`.

rachael: note: when keys are renamed we also lose deterministic KV cache ordering for chat runtime which can subtly change output on long contexts. even if loss is small, it affects safety/eval metrics. we should ensure remap keeps canonical ordering.

patrick: next steps: (1) merge PR #3421; (2) run conversion again with `--preserve-special-tokens`; (3) run quantization experiments with both group sizes and record evaluation diffs on our assistant eval set; (4) add integration test that simulates hub index vs shards race. i'll take (1) & (4).

maria: thanks — assigning follow-ups in the ticket. i'll re-run the evals after PR deploy and post results here. :thumbsup:
